jp: 田中[たなか]さん{は|wa-topic}学生[がくせい]です。山田[やまだ]さん{も|mo-also}学生[がくせい]です。
en: Mr. Tanaka is a student. Mr. Yamada is a student too.
why: Adding a second person with the same status ('too') is も; は would present Mr. Yamada as a contrast.

jp: 朝[あさ]パン{を|o-object}食[た]べました。昼[ひる]{も|mo-also}パン{を|o-object}食[た]べました。
en: I ate bread in the morning. I ate bread at noon too.
why: The same thing happened again at noon, so も adds it to the morning; は would contrast the two times.

jp: 兄[あに]{は|wa-topic}テニス{が|ga-stative}上手[じょうず]です。弟[おとうと]{も|mo-also}上手[じょうず]です。
en: My older brother is good at tennis. My younger brother is good at it too.
why: The younger brother shares the same quality as the older one, so も adds him to the set.

jp: 田中[たなか]さん{は/が|wa-topic}来[き]ませんでした。山田[やまだ]さん{も|mo-also}来[き]ませんでした。
en: Mr. Tanaka didn't come. Mr. Yamada didn't come either.
why: 'Either' adds another person to the same negative fact, and that is も even with a negative verb.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}雨[あめ]{が|ga-subject}降[ふ]っています。風[かぜ]{も|mo-also}強[つよ]いです。
en: It is raining today. The wind is strong too.
why: The wind is a second thing added to the rain, so it takes も.

jp: 私[わたし]{の|no-possessive}父[ちち]{も|mo-both}母[はは]{も|mo-both}先生[せんせい]です。
en: My father and my mother are both teachers.
why: In a 'both A and B' pair every noun gets も; 父は母も would break the pair and lose 'both'.

jp: 母[はは]{は|wa-topic}コーヒー{を|o-object}飲[の]みます。父[ちち]{も|mo-also}飲[の]みます。
en: My mother drinks coffee. My father does too.
why: The father does the same as the mother, so も adds him; は would make it a contrast.

jp: この本[ほん]{は|wa-topic}面白[おもしろ]いです。その本[ほん]{も|mo-also}面白[おもしろ]いです。
en: This book is interesting. That book is interesting too.
why: A second book with the same quality is added with も.

jp: 昨日[きのう]{は|wa-topic}雨[あめ]でした。今日[きょう]{も|mo-also}雨[あめ]です。
en: It was rainy yesterday. It is rainy today too.
why: Today repeats yesterday's weather, so も adds the second day.

jp: 駅[えき]{の|no-possessive}近[ちか]く{に|ni-location}コンビニ{が|ga-existence}あります。銀行[ぎんこう]{も|mo-also}あります。
en: There is a convenience store near the station. There is a bank too.
why: The bank is another thing that exists there, so も adds it to the store.

jp: 友達[ともだち]{と|to-with}映画[えいが]{を|o-object}見[み]ました。そのあと、買[か]い物[もの]{も|mo-also}しました。
en: I watched a movie with a friend. After that I went shopping as well.
why: Shopping is one more activity added to the movie, so も fits; は would not mean 'as well'.

jp: 英語[えいご]{も|mo-both}日本語[にほんご]{も|mo-both}話[はな]せます。
en: I can speak both English and Japanese.
why: A 'both A and B' pair needs も after each noun; 英語は would set English apart instead of pairing it.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}土曜日[どようび]です。明日[あした]{も|mo-also}休[やす]みです。
en: Today is Saturday. Tomorrow is a day off too.
why: Tomorrow is added to today as another day off, so も is used.

jp: 鈴木[すずき]さん{は|wa-topic}パーティー{に|ni-destination}行[い]きます。佐藤[さとう]さん{も|mo-also}行[い]きます{か|ka-question}。
en: Mr. Suzuki is going to the party. Is Mr. Sato going too?
why: The question asks whether Mr. Sato joins Mr. Suzuki, which is 'too', so も is used.

jp: この店[みせ]{の|no-possessive}ラーメン{は|wa-topic}おいしいです{ね|ne-agreement}。ぎょうざ{も|mo-also}おいしいです{よ|yo-assertion}。
en: This shop's ramen is delicious, isn't it? The gyoza is delicious too.
why: The gyoza is added to the ramen as another delicious item, so も is used.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}ゲーム{を|o-object}しません。妹[いもうと]{も|mo-also}しません。
en: I don't play video games. My little sister doesn't either.
why: The sister shares the same negative fact, so も adds her.

jp: スーパー{で|de-place}パン{を|o-object}買[か]いました。牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]{も|mo-also}買[か]いました。
en: I bought bread at the supermarket. I bought milk as well.
why: Milk is another item bought, added to the bread with も.

jp: 夏休[なつやす]み{に|ni-time}北海道[ほっかいどう]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きました。沖縄[おきなわ]{に/へ|ni-destination}{も|mo-also}行[い]きました。
en: I went to Hokkaido in the summer vacation. I went to Okinawa too.
why: Okinawa is another place visited besides Hokkaido, so も is added after に to mean 'too'.

jp: 暑[あつ]いです{ね|ne-agreement}。私[わたし]{も|mo-also}そう思[おも]います。
en: It's hot, isn't it? I think so too.
why: The speaker agrees with the same opinion, so 'I too' is 私も.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{も|mo-both}妹[いもうと]{も|mo-both}犬[いぬ]{が|ga-stative}好[す]きです。
en: My younger brother and my younger sister both like dogs.
why: A 'both A and B' pair needs も after each noun; は on the first noun breaks the pair.

jp: 公園[こうえん]{に|ni-location}子[こ]どもたち{が|ga-existence}います。犬[いぬ]{も|mo-also}います。
en: There are children in the park. There are dogs too.
why: Dogs are one more thing present in the park, so も adds them.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}ごみ{を|o-object}出[だ]しました。明日[あした]{も|mo-also}出[だ]します。
en: I took out the trash today. I will take it out tomorrow too.
why: The same action is repeated tomorrow, so も adds the second day.

jp: 田中[たなか]さん{は|wa-topic}ピアノ{を|o-object}弾[ひ]きます。ギター{も|mo-also}弾[ひ]きます。
en: Mr. Tanaka plays the piano. He plays the guitar too.
why: The guitar is a second instrument he plays, added with も.

jp: 今[いま]、お金[かね]{が/は|ga-existence}ありません。時間[じかん]{も|mo-also}ありません。
en: I have no money right now. I have no time either.
why: Time is added to money as one more thing missing, so も is used.

jp: 雪[ゆき]{が|ga-subject}降[ふ]りました。電車[でんしゃ]{も|mo-also}止[と]まりました。
en: It snowed, and the trains stopped as well.
why: The train stoppage is one more event added to the snow, so も is used.

jp: 図書館[としょかん]{で|de-place}本[ほん]{を|o-object}借[か]りました。雑誌[ざっし]{も|mo-also}借[か]りました。
en: I borrowed a book at the library. I borrowed a magazine too.
why: The magazine is another item borrowed, so も adds it.

jp: 学校[がっこう]{は|wa-topic}九時[くじ]{に|ni-time}始[はじ]まります。会社[かいしゃ]{も|mo-also}九時[くじ]{に|ni-time}始[はじ]まります。
en: School starts at nine. Work at the company starts at nine too.
why: The company shares the same start time, so も adds it to the school.

jp: 彼女[かのじょ]{は|wa-topic}英語[えいご]{を|o-object}話[はな]します。フランス語[ご]{も|mo-also}話[はな]します。
en: She speaks English. She speaks French too.
why: French is a second language she speaks, added with も.

jp: 冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]{に|ni-location}牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]{が|ga-existence}あります。卵[たまご]{も|mo-also}あります。
en: There is milk in the fridge. There are eggs too.
why: Eggs are one more item in the fridge, so も adds them to the milk.

jp: 兄[あに]{は|wa-topic}タバコ{を|o-object}吸[す]いません。父[ちち]{も|mo-also}吸[す]いません。
en: My older brother doesn't smoke. My father doesn't either.
why: The father shares the same negative fact, so も adds him.

jp: 月曜日[げつようび]{は|wa-contrast}忙[いそが]しいです。日曜日[にちようび]{は|wa-contrast}ひまです。
en: I am busy on Mondays. On Sundays I am free.
why: Busy and free are opposites, so the two days are contrasted with は; も would claim the same state.

jp: コーヒー{は|wa-contrast}飲[の]めます。でも、お酒[さけ]{は|wa-contrast}飲[の]めません。
en: I can drink coffee. But I can't drink alcohol.
why: The two drinks are set against each other with は; も would mean 'alcohol too', which does not fit.

jp: うち{の|no-possessive}犬[いぬ]{は|wa-contrast}水[みず]{が|ga-stative}好[す]きです。でも、猫[ねこ]{は|wa-contrast}水[みず]{が|ga-stative}嫌[きら]いです。
en: Our dog likes water. But our cat hates water.
why: Liking and hating are opposites, so the cat is contrasted with は; も would say it likes water too.

jp: この道[みち]{は|wa-contrast}安全[あんぜん]です。あの道[みち]{は|wa-contrast}危[あぶ]ないです。
en: This road is safe. That road is dangerous.
why: Safe and dangerous are opposites, so は contrasts the two roads.

jp: 泳[およ]ぐ{の|no-nominalizer}{は|wa-contrast}得意[とくい]です。走[はし]る{の|no-nominalizer}{は|wa-contrast}苦手[にがて]です。
en: I am good at swimming. I am bad at running.
why: Good at and bad at are opposites, so the two activities are contrasted with は.

jp: 日本語[にほんご]{は|wa-contrast}話[はな]せます。でも、中国語[ちゅうごくご]{は|wa-contrast}話[はな]せません。
en: I can speak Japanese. But I can't speak Chinese.
why: The ability is set against the lack of it, so は marks the contrast; も would mean 'Chinese too'.

jp: 電車[でんしゃ]{は|wa-contrast}速[はや]いです。でも、バス{は|wa-contrast}遅[おそ]いです。
en: The train is fast. But the bus is slow.
why: Fast and slow are opposites, so は contrasts the train with the bus.

jp: 昼[ひる]{は|wa-contrast}暖[あたた]かいです。でも、夜[よる]{は|wa-contrast}寒[さむ]いです。
en: It is warm in the daytime. But at night it is cold.
why: Warm and cold are opposites, so は contrasts day and night.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は|wa-contrast}野菜[やさい]{を|o-object}食[た]べます。妹[いもうと]{は|wa-contrast}野菜[やさい]{を|o-object}食[た]べません。
en: My younger brother eats vegetables, but my younger sister doesn't.
why: Eating and not eating are opposites; も would say the sister doesn't eat them either, which contradicts the brother.

jp: 試験[しけん]{は|wa-contrast}簡単[かんたん]でした。でも、宿題[しゅくだい]{は|wa-contrast}難[むずか]しかったです。
en: The exam was easy. But the homework was difficult.
why: Easy and difficult are opposites, so は contrasts the exam with the homework.

jp: この部屋[へや]{は|wa-contrast}広[ひろ]いです。あの部屋[へや]{は|wa-contrast}狭[せま]いです。
en: This room is big. That room is small.
why: Big and small are opposites, so は contrasts the two rooms.

jp: ひらがな{は|wa-contrast}読[よ]めます。でも、漢字[かんじ]{は|wa-contrast}読[よ]めません。
en: I can read hiragana. But I can't read kanji.
why: The ability is set against the lack of it, so は marks the contrast; も would mean 'kanji too'.

jp: 野球[やきゅう]{は|wa-contrast}好[す]きです。サッカー{は|wa-contrast}嫌[きら]いです。
en: I like baseball. I dislike soccer.
why: Like and dislike are opposites, so は contrasts the two sports.

jp: 鳥[とり]{は|wa-contrast}飛[と]べます。でも、犬[いぬ]{は|wa-contrast}飛[と]べません。
en: Birds can fly. But dogs can't.
why: Can and cannot are opposites, so は contrasts birds and dogs; も would say dogs can't either, which is false.

jp: 今[いま]{は|wa-contrast}ひまです。でも、午後[ごご]{は|wa-contrast}忙[いそが]しいです。
en: I am free now. But in the afternoon I am busy.
why: Free and busy are opposites, so は contrasts the two times.
